subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept a custom compatibility-preserving glob walker and cooperative bootstrap-hook scheduling in the core embedded-run hot path, or should the responsiveness fix use a smaller owner-designed scheduling boundary?
rationale: This is a deliberate runtime-policy tradeoff between responsiveness and exact established bootstrap-file and hook timing semantics; tests and the benchmark cannot determine which compatibility boundary maintainers want to guarantee.

options.title: Accept the bounded runtime policy
options.body: Approve the custom walker and bootstrap-only scheduling change after exact-head CI completes, treating the current parity tests as the supported compatibility contract.

options.title: Narrow the scheduling fix
options.body: Keep asynchronous root reads and a smaller cooperative checkpoint, but ask for an owner-designed approach that continues to use Node glob semantics rather than maintaining a parallel matcher.

options.title: Pause for broader runtime design
options.body: Defer this PR if the team wants the broader gateway responsiveness work to define shared scheduling and observability conventions first.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded runtime policy
recommendation.body: Approve the custom walker and bootstrap-only scheduling change after exact-head CI completes, treating the current parity tests as the supported compatibility contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline identifies steipete as a directly notified decision-maker, and the remaining question is runtime compatibility policy rather than a mechanical patch repair.
